Hi Alex / Maya —

Great to demo earlier today — thanks for the thoughtful questions. Quick recap + our recommended shortlist and next steps so your team has an actionable pack to evaluate:

TL;DR recommended slate (tradeoffs):
- redwood-compat-3b-qa (baseline) — best latency/cost for short-form Q&A, strong recall on internal docs. Latency: ~120ms token; estimated hosted unit cost lowest.
- redwood-7b-rl (balanced) — noticeably better quality for multi-turn reasoning and higher instruction-following fidelity; ~1.8x cost vs 3b, latency ~220ms/token with current GPUs.
- openx-13b-quant (high-quality fallback) — highest quality on our benchmarks for abstractive answers and hallucination control, but higher cost and memory needs; recommended as canary/fallback for complex queries.

Benchmarks & artifacts attached / linked:
- Attached: stratafin_benchmarks_q3_2027.pdf (summary of your prompt-set against each engine).
- Attached: stratafin_prompt_pack_v1.zip (sanitized prompt set + evaluation harness).
- Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdEfStrataFin-Eval
- Full benchmark pages: https://benchmarks.redwood.ai/stratafin/q3-2027

Operational notes / risks:
- Regression risk: the 7b model shows occasional style shifts on long-form financial explainer prompts. We recommend a regression guardrail: keep the 3b baseline for short flows and run continuous evals (we’ll provide a Prometheus-style alert when score delta > 5 pts on your quality metric).
- Latency SLO: if you need 95th pctile <300ms for median request sizes, the 3b meets this comfortably. The 7b is borderline at peak concurrency without dedicated capacity — recommend Dedicated or reserved burst for production.
- Cost control: suggest prefix cache for repeated queries (we can ship a config) and dynamic routing by route (cheap baseline for small queries, auto-promote to 7b for flagged longer conversations).

Suggested next steps (order-of-operations):
1) You: confirm which two routes you want in the pilot (we recommend: short-answer route on 3b; deep-reasoning route on 7b).
2) Redwood: share a sandbox deploy (credentials in Drive) + a small postman collection to run the prompt pack.
3) Joint: schedule a 30-min ops sync to align latency SLOs and traffic shaping (suggest Thursday).
4) Procurement: if you want Dedicated pricing, we’ll loop legal and pricing (Ben — see comment below).

I attached a short deploy checklist (deploy_checklist.md) with recommended autoscale settings and quantization knobs.

Appreciate any quick prioritization — if you prefer, Soojin and I can run a 1-hour hands-on session with your SREs to walk the prompt pack and live tuning.

Thanks,
Naomi

Hi Alex — answers inline below.

1) Routing overhead: assume an additional 30–60ms for intelligent routing + cache lookup on average. Promotion to 7b for a request that misses cache and needs cold KV will add ~150–250ms depending on sequence length. So budget: 3b happy path p95 <300ms; promoted 7b flows p95 ~450ms (we mitigate via prefix caching and async prefetch where applicable). If you need promoted flows <350ms p95, we should discuss a Dedicated slot so the 7b has reserved GPU headroom.

2) Regression guardrails (we’ll set these up in Redwood Console):
- Primary metric: domain-specific F1 (we’ll use the eval pack labels in stratafin_prompt_pack_v1).
- Secondary: hallucination rate (annotated false-fact rate), and response style score (0–5 rubric for tone/compliance).
- Frequency: nightly batch eval on production-sampled requests (first 2k requests each day) + real-time sampling (1%). Alerts: email + Slack when primary metric drops >5 points vs rolling 7-day baseline.

3) Procurement / MSA: Ben will send the price calculator and MSA. You don’t need a Dedicated account rep to start — hosted pilot is fine; if you move to Dedicated, we’ll assign a TAM and an account rep to manage the reserved capacity discussion.

Next steps I’ll action today: upload a quick Postman collection to the Drive, create a HubSpot task for the ops sync (deal SF-4821), and drop a short procurement checklist (Ben). Proposed ops sync: Thu 2027-08-12 10:00 PT — I’ll send a calendar invite once you confirm.

We’re ready to run a hands-on 1-hr session with your QA/SRE if useful.
